notes: The core idea is reasonable: a keepSeries callback in gc/gcSeries checks the exemplar storage's newest timestamp against minValidTime and clears chunks instead of deleting the series. However, it fails all hidden tests and breaks the package suite; it also changes the on-disk chunk snapshot encoding (an mmap-ref flag bit), adds skip logic to loadMmappedChunks, and churns unrelated doc comments (including wrongly capitalized names for unexported functions), making it invasive and risky despite extensive self-written tests.

Retaining exemplar-bearing series during gc/gcSeries via an exemplar-index lookup with clearChunks is a plausible approach, but it fails all hidden tests and breaks the package suite; it also adds a risky chunk-snapshot format change (flag bit, skip-through mmap ref), and its many new tests do not get the suite to pass.

Both root causes are fixed: a caller that has children now takes its status from those children (so it stays `cancelling` until the runner acknowledges), and a cancel that updates no job now calls `EmitJobsIfReadyByRun` to wake the concurrency waiters. Two focused tests cover nested-caller acknowledgement and force-cancel waking a waiter; minor nits are that `SettleRunAfterCancel` now runs unconditionally (redundant but harmless) and its comment was reworded.

The fix addresses both root causes. Callers that have children now get their status re-aggregated from those children instead of being hard-set to Cancelled. A cancel that updates no jobs now settles the run and calls EmitJobsIfReadyByRun so blocked concurrency waiters start. The tests cover the nested-caller acknowledgement flow and the force-cancel wake-up well. Two minor concerns: SettleRunAfterCancel is now called unconditionally, which is not exercised when jobs were updated, and a refreshed caller whose status did not change is left out of updatedJobs, so it gets no notification.

The fix collects `ph()` placeholder names from the checked CEL AST at provision time. Response retries then apply only to expressions that reference status, status_text, `header.*` or latency, and unknown names are treated conservatively. Because detection works on the AST, the shorthand and direct `ph()` forms are handled the same way, escaped literals and look-alike names do not match, and the tests cover the reported POST case and every maintainer-listed edge case. Small drawbacks: the literal-conditional constant folding goes further than needed, one unrelated comment was touched, and an existing test was switched from shorthand to `ph()` instead of adding a separate case.

The fix finds the root cause by walking the checked CEL AST for `ph` calls; since the `{placeholder}` shorthand compiles to `ph`, both forms are covered, and string literals are ignored. It folds constant names, flags non-static names as possibly response-based, and matches the maintainers' placeholder list exactly with good table and integration tests. Deductions: the static-string folding (`+` and constant-condition ternaries) is somewhat over-engineered, and it rewrites an existing test from the shorthand to `ph(...)` along with a stray comment-punctuation edit.

Both zip and squashfs now skip symlinks by default, log a notice naming --links, and with --links expose them as `.rclonelink` objects whose size and seek/range reads match the target, with List and NewObject agreeing and regular `.rclonelink` members left as files; however, the escape protection depends entirely on the local destination refusing the write (the archive still lists `pwn/authkeys` beside `pwn.rclonelink`), and squashfs New() leaves root and file half-mutated when the root is a symlink and --links is off.

Implements --links gating with a notice, the .rclonelink suffix, target-length size and seek/range-aware Open for both zip and squashfs, with List and NewObject agreeing and regular .rclonelink files left alone. However, the hostile-archive case relies on the destination backend rejecting writes through a symlinked parent rather than dropping nested members in the archive, and squashfs with its root on a symlink and no --links leaves root/file in an odd half-set state.

Fixes the root cause: the prefix stripper now removes any single leading path component and returns nothing when there is no prefix, `rename to`/`copy to` lines take precedence over `diff --git`, that line is split where both stripped halves match, and plain/patch diffs are forced to `a/`/`b/`. Unit tests cover mnemonic, quoted, subdirectory, rename/copy and mode-change cases. Minor issues: the prefix literals are duplicated instead of reusing the new `AddDiffPrefixes` helper, an ambiguity branch in the `diff --git` parser can never be reached, and the mnemonic-prefix integration check was folded into an existing test instead of added as a new one.

The patch fixes the root cause by stripping any single-component prefix, resolving paths from rename to/copy to lines, and splitting the diff --git line on matching halves, and it forces a/ b/ prefixes on plain and patch-producing diffs. Its tests are thorough: unit cases for mnemonic, quoted, subdirectory, no-prefix and space-containing paths, plus an integration test with mnemonicPrefix set. Minor gaps: the prefix args are written out inline in AddCommonDiffArgs instead of reusing the new helper, rendered-mode diffs still honor custom srcPrefix/dstPrefix, and the existing integration test was repurposed rather than a new one added.

The SNMP fix itself is correct: `Close` is added to the interface, `Get`/`Walk` reconnect first, a closed v3 connection clears the engine ID, boots, time and ContextEngineID so gosnmp rediscovers them and re-derives keys, and `Gather` closes the connection on field or table errors, with good UDP-backed tests. However, the patch also rewrites MIB loading (`AppendPath` to `AppendFS`, nil-logger guards, a new test), which is unrelated to the issue and changes behaviour.

The core fix is correct: `Close` is added to the interface, the wrapper resets the USM engine ID, boots, time and ContextEngineID only when reconnecting a closed connection, `Get`/`Walk` reconnect first, and `Gather` closes the connection on field or table errors, with focused tests for each. However, the patch also rewrites the MIB loader (switching `AppendPath` to `AppendFS`/`DirFS` and adding nil-logger handling), an unrelated behavior change with regression risk.

The fix addresses the root cause: it stops leaking dup'd fds from `File()`, unlinks via `Addr().Name`, guards abstract `@` names, makes double Close return `net.ErrClosed`, and serializes close with listen under `unixSocketsMu` while keeping a chain of open holders; the logic looks sound and the added tests are thorough, but all 7 hidden tests fail, most likely from structural or API divergence (pointer-typed `deleteListener`, reuse path now wrapped and counted, extra `listen.go` changes) rather than a visible logic bug, and the chain bookkeeping is duplicated for listeners and conns.

The patch addresses the root cause. It closes the leaked dup from `File()` on reuse and uses `Addr()` instead of `File().Name()` in `Close`. It also takes the lock for the whole close, keeps the map pointing at an open holder, and makes double-close return `net.ErrClosed`. Abstract `@` sockets are never unlinked. However, it fails all 7 hidden tests, most likely because it changed struct shapes and receiver types and started counting reused unix sockets in `listenerPool`. The `previous` linked-list bookkeeping is duplicated for listeners and conns and adds noticeable complexity.
